summary: A fiction excerpt (Book 10, part 150) in which Ria explains to Leon how a powerful figure named Viktor spent about eight billion rupiah to engineer quieter jetpacks and fake consumer-protection lawsuits forcing recalls, stressing that power rather than money is what matters and that the Viktor group does not use assassination. The scene then moves to a rooftop co-op bar with a conservatory of limes and mint, where Ria, a member who worked off her membership by planting trees, admits she earns a lot of money. The note is cut off mid-scene.
one_line: Ria explains to Leon how Viktor engineered quieter jetpacks through staged lawsuits, then they drink daiquiris at a rooftop co-op bar.
key_facts: Ria says Viktor's group spent about eight billion in the end on a project to make the skies quieter.
The group staged consumer-protection lawsuits to 'force' a recall of the loud jetpacks.
The recalled jetpacks were rebuilt with pipes engineered and tuned so they could be used for the woodwinds section.
Ria says the project let everyone get what they wanted: fast rides, quiet skies, safe and cheap vehicles, which she calls 'Win win win.'
Ria says buying laws or buying out competitors would have been possible but were 'very, you know, blunt.'
Ria says 'The sums are just a convenient way of directing power. Power is what matters.'
Ria tells Leon, 'We don't use assassination,' when he jokes about Viktor ninjas.
An old school flyer with a loud jetpack roars past, and Ria says he will be machining his own replacement parts because no one makes them anymore.
The rooftop conservatory's limes are juiced by the barman over his blender to make daiquiris.
Ria says you cannot buy your way into the rooftop bar; you have to work it off because it is a co-op.
Ria says she planted the row of trees and the mint garden on the rooftop.
Ria admits, unembarrassed, that she earns a lot of money when Leon asks about it.
